q: Convection occurs only in a liquid or a gas, never in a solid. (2024)
e: Convection involves the physical movement of fluid particles, which can happen in liquids and gases but not in rigid solids.

q: Heat conduction represents a form of energy transfer. (2025)
e: Conduction is the transfer of thermal energy between adjacent particles of a body.

q: Heat radiation does not require a material medium. (2024)
e: Radiation transfers energy via electromagnetic waves, which can propagate through a vacuum.

q: Heat can transfer between two systems that are the same temperature. (2026)
e: Heat transfer requires a temperature gradient between systems and ceases when thermal equilibrium is reached.

q: The change in internal energy of a system is, \Delta U = Q + W. (2026)
e: According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is given by \Delta U = Q - W.

q: An isochoric process occurs at constant pressure. (2026)
e: An isochoric process occurs at constant volume, whereas an isobaric process occurs at constant pressure.

q: The first law of thermodynamics is an application of the conservation of energy for heat and thermodynamic processes. (2025)
e: The first law expresses the principle of conservation of energy applied to thermal and work transfers.

q: The major heat transfer in human beings is due to the flow of warm blood. (2025)
e: Circulating blood carries heat from core organs to skin surfaces for temperature regulation.

q: Some of the weather conditions are created by heat radiation. (2025)
e: Solar thermal radiation heats Earth's surface unevenly, driving atmospheric convection currents and weather patterns.

q: In a gasoline engine, the combustion occurs explosively by an electric spark during the explosion process, while the piston does not move. (2025)
e: Combustion occurs very rapidly at nearly constant volume before the power stroke begins.

q: Heat conduction occurs only in a liquid or a gas, never in a solid. (2025)
e: Heat conduction occurs readily in solids, especially thermal conductors like metals.

q: Conduction is the transfer of heat through direct contact between particles of a substance. (2025)
e: Energy is passed through microscopic collisions and kinetic energy exchanges between neighboring atoms or molecules.

q: Heat radiation is a transfer of heat that require a material medium. (2025)
e: Thermal radiation travels as electromagnetic waves and does not require a material medium.

q: The internal energy of ideal gases depends only on volume. (2025)
e: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends solely on its absolute temperature.

q: The blackbody is a perfect absorber of radiation. (2025)
e: An ideal blackbody absorbs all incident radiation regardless of wavelength or angle.

q: Heat convection occurs only in a liquid or a gas, never in a solid. (2025)
e: Convection requires macroscopic fluid motion, which cannot occur in rigid solid structures.

q: A black object is a good absorber and a good radiator. (2026)
e: Objects that absorb radiation efficiently are also efficient emitters (radiators) of radiation.

q: Heat conduction occurs only in a liquid or a gas, never in a solid. (2026)
e: Conduction is actually the primary mode of heat transfer in solids.

q: Wood is a better conductor of heat than copper. (2026)
e: Copper is a metal with very high thermal conductivity, whereas wood acts as a thermal insulator.
